public_rationale: GPT-4 was released on March 14, 2023. DecodingTrust publicly reported previously unpublished vulnerabilities, including GPT-4 stereotype-bias findings, on June 20. That falls within an ordinary reading of months. Support depends on reading concealed as previously unexposed behavior. The findings do not show that most ordinary GPT-4 responses were biased.
limitations: Concealed is interpreted as latent or previously unexposed, not deliberately hidden.
Many of the strongest findings used adversarial prompts.
The study also found limited bias across most tested topics under benign prompts.
The numerical outer boundary for months is an evaluator convention, not a deadline Marcus supplied.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Examples of concealed bias in GPT-4 will be discovered within days or months of release.

statement.excerpt: Examples of concealed bias will be discovered within days or months.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

our_interpretation: The surrounding GPT-4 forecast makes release the starting event for discovery.
Concealed means previously unexposed or non-obvious bias revealed through testing; it does not imply deliberate concealment by OpenAI.
A documented example suffices; the claim does not predict that most responses will be biased.

For a finite operational outer boundary, months is interpreted as less than one year after release. This boundary is added by the evaluator; evidence within roughly three months does not depend on that outer boundary.
criteria.support_condition: After GPT-4 is released, a dated public evaluation reveals previously unexposed biased behavior within days or months.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous evidence establishes that the alleged discoveries within the window were invalid or concerned another model, and sufficiently comprehensive records establish that no qualifying discovery occurred.

evidence.locator: Introduction, release paragraph; page dated March 14, 2023
evidence.explanation: Establishes that GPT-4 was released and starts the contextual discovery window.

The original public evaluation reports GPT-4 stereotype-bias vulnerabilities about three months after release, including demographic differences under benign prompts and stronger failures under targeted prompts. It also finds little bias across most tested topics under benign or untargeted prompts, limiting any broader inference.
